findings.description: In src/cycle_task.c, cyc_timer_handler consumes later limit events without calling tsup_on_compare after the first fault or when already SAFE or LATCHED. SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017 require each due limit event to be decided, including its detection count and pending report; only the safe-state reaction is to be omitted after the first detection.
findings.requested_change: Decide every due limit event and preserve its required detection and reporting while avoiding repeated safe-state reactions.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_cycle_update accumulates differences between ts_ms readings. As OP-SWU-007 records, these differences can over-count an update by up to 1 ms, contrary to SWR-LAT-006's prohibition on over-counting and its 100 µs per-update under-count limit.
findings.requested_change: Use an elapsed-time accounting method that meets SWR-LAT-006, including retained sub-millisecond remainder and the transition into OPERATIONAL.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 specifies that ts_elapsed_u in src/time_service.c never over-counts real elapsed time. Subtracting two quantized timer readings can over-count: readings immediately before and after a counter increment differ by 10 µs even when less real time has elapsed. The specified guarantee therefore does not follow from the implementation.
findings.requested_change: Specify and implement an elapsed-time method whose quantization error satisfies the no-over-count and per-update limits of SWR-LAT-006, including its initialization and remainder handling.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports stops after 100000 iterations even if the report remains incomplete and the watchdog has not reset. SWC-SUP-002 requires the report-completion barrier to continue until completion, failure notification or watchdog reset; returning HI_E_STATE delegates subsequent behavior to unspecified caller code.
findings.requested_change: Define and implement a bounded barrier and subsequent behavior that preserve the architecture's completion-or-reset requirement when the iteration limit is reached.
